To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystal structure of the yeast tRNA(PHe) has been determined at 2. 00 A resolution using data from 15 year old single crystals.

the crystal structure of the tRNA is now known to higher accuracy, that there is a novel geometry for Mg(2+) binding to the tRNA, that there is an unusual spermine molecule in the crystal lattice, and that the tRNA has been cleaved by the presence of the Mg(2+).
the crystal structure of the yeast tRNA(P) at 2. 00 A resolution reveals a novel water structure around Mg(2+) and also shows that two regions of the tRNAs in the crystals are cleaved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the yeast phenylalaninyl-tRNA synthetase and the tRNA(Phe).
the structure of RNA, in particular tRNA.
understanding the structure and function of the tRNA molecule, and in particular the role of metal ions in the structure and in tRNA function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Mg(2+) ions are essential to the tRNA structure and that the metal ions can be involved in the hydrolysis of the tRNA molecule.
the crystal structure is a snapshot of an ensemble of tRNA molecules in which the metal ions are tightly bound and the tRNA molecules are partially cleaved, but still largely intact.

the crystal structure of the yeast phenylalaninel -tRNA is well determined, and that the structure of the Mg(2+)-bound tRNA has been refined to a level where it is now possible to make more accurate statements on the geometry of Mg(2+) binding and the role of the water molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure determination of tRNA has reached a stage at which the structure is so well defined that we can see the effect of cleavage on the tRNA structure.
the structure is now more accurate and the interpretation of the structure more complete, with a more detailed description of the Mg(2+) -binding sites.
the crystal structure is now well established and the new structure can be used as a reference for further studies of RNA-ligand interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the structure of yeast tRNAPhe at 2. 00 Å resolution, determined using 15-year old data, is of high quality, and that this structure provides a more accurate description of the tRNA and the metal binding sites than previous work.
